<b>Ko izdaje atest i da li je u ceni?</b: Who issues the test certificate, and is it included in the price? Without a test certificate you have no document for the building, the garage owner or the insurer.

<b>Ko meri struju i kako se plaća?</b> U: Who meters the electricity and how is it paid for? In an apartment building or a rented garage this is question number one. The answer is a MID-certified meter and billing at the price on the electricity bill — details in the electricity guide.
<b>Ko priprema papire za skupštinu?</b>: Who prepares the paperwork for the residents' assembly? Technical specification, draft decision and agenda item — either you get them, or you write them yourself. How the procedure works.

<b>Koja zaštita se ugrađuje</b>Punjaču t: Which protection is installedThe charger needs a type A RCD combined with 6 mA DC fault current detection in the charger itself, or a type B RCD; an ordinary type AC RCD is not enough. The explanation is in the safety and test certificate guide.
<b>Koji presek kabla i kolika dužina?</b: What cable cross-section and what length? It should be written in the quote; “it will be enough” is not an answer.
<b>Koju zaštitu ugrađujete?</b> Za punja: What protection do you install? A charger needs a type A RCD with 6 mA DC detection (or type B) and its own circuit breaker. An ordinary Schuko socket and an extension cord are not the answer — why, explained here.
<b>Koliko kW prima vaš auto</b>Na naizme: How many kW your car acceptsOn alternating current (AC), most cars accept between 7 and 11 kW — the specifications list it as the power of the on-board charger. A 22 kW charger will not charge faster than that.

<strong>1. Na oko — nema merenja.</stron: 1. Guesswork — no metering. The charger goes on the shared meter and the cost is spread across all flats through the homeowners' association bill. For the building this is the easiest option while there are no cars; with the first car it becomes a matter of passing one person's costs on to the neighbours, and with the third it shows up on the bill. This is also the most common source of arguments at the residents' assembly.
<strong>11 ili 22 kW.</strong> Skoro svi: 11 or 22 kW. Almost all cars in Serbia accept at most 11 kW of alternating current, and a typical home installation has ⟦0⟧ kW of approved power anyway (3×25 A). A 22 kW charger does not charge any faster if the car cannot take it.
<strong>2. Paušal.</strong> Skupština od: 2. Flat fee. The assembly sets a fixed monthly amount per car. It is only as fair as the estimate is accurate: if the flat fee is lower than the actual consumption, everyone still pays the difference; if it is higher, the car owner pays more than they use. A flat fee makes sense as a temporary solution until a meter is installed.
<strong>3. Brojilo (MID).</strong> Overe: 3. Meter (MID). A certified meter measures only that space, and the cost is re-invoiced to the owner at the price on the building's bill — with no markup. It is also the cleanest option legally: the building does not resell electricity but passes on a cost, which matters because of Article 210v of the Energy Law. The equipment costs ⟦0⟧–⟦1⟧ RSD today, and some chargers have a meter built in.
<strong>ABB Terra AC 22 kW</strong>: naj: ABB Terra AC 22 kW: the widest range in the register — ⟦0⟧ RSD (Tehnodućan, with RFID and 4G, online discount, down from ⟦1⟧), ⟦2⟧ (Jakov Sistem, on sale, down from ⟦3⟧), ⟦4⟧ (Elektronapon, without cable) and ⟦5⟧ (Bazzar, with RFID and 4G). The model codes are not the same, so the devices are not the same either — the difference is in the cable, RFID and the 4G module — but a price difference of several times over is reason enough to compare the exact model codes before buying.
<strong>ABB Terra AC W22-T-R-C-0</strong: ABB Terra AC W22-T-R-C-0: ⟦0⟧ RSD (Tehnodućan), ⟦1⟧ RSD (Jakov Sistem) — a difference of ⟦2⟧ RSD.

<strong>Atest i merenja.</strong> Dokume: Test certificate (atest) and measurements. A document from a licensed contractor confirming that the installation was carried out and measured in line with regulations (SRPS HD 60364-6). In the table it is specifically mentioned only by Emobility (“measurements and issuing of measurement results”) and by us. Without a test certificate you have neither proof of safety nor an argument for the building and the insurer.

<strong>Brojilo u uređaju (MID).</strong: Meter in the device (MID). If the charger is in a shared garage and the electricity is billed on to residents, certified (MID) billing is required. <strong>Brojilo, papiri i ono posle.</st: Meter, paperwork and what comes after. If you live in an apartment building or rent a garage, the device is the least of your problems: the question is who pays for the electricity and what the residents' assembly says. No charger solves that on its own — a MID-certified meter, monthly billing and documents for the assembly meeting do. Going by the public websites we checked on ⟦0⟧, we are the only ones offering this as a service — and that is why we cost more than a device from a web shop.

<strong>Dinamičko ograničenje snage (DLB: Dynamic power limiting (DLB). The charger reduces the current by itself when the cooker and water heater are switched on in the flat, so the main breaker does not trip. With older installations this is often a cheaper solution than increasing the approved (contracted) power — this, and why 22 kW rarely makes sense in practice, is covered in the guide how much a charger costs.
<strong>Dinamičko upravljanje snagom</st: Dynamic load management on 11 kW wallboxes: a sensor at the supply connection monitors household consumption and reduces the charging power when the cooker and water heater are switched on — so the main breaker does not trip.

<strong>Javni punjači:</strong> kWh koje: Public chargers: kWh the car receives × price per kWh. Operators in Serbia bill per minute, so the price per kWh is a calculation: the average of four receipts from the Charge&GO app, August–September 2026 (43–79 RSD/kWh).

<strong>Kako to radi Evolako.</strong> N: How Evolako does it. We do not sell electricity — we measure it. We charge for the equipment, the installation and the service, not for kilowatts. A MID-certified meter is included in every package, and billing is at the price on the EPS bill of whoever owns the meter the electricity runs through, with no markup. A monthly statement document goes to you and to the owner or building manager; the first 2 months are free, after that it is part of the ⟦0⟧ RSD subscription.

Druga stvar koja se ne vidi: punjač u au: The second thing you cannot see: the car's on-board charger can let direct (DC) leakage current into the installation. An ordinary type AC RCD does not see this current, and in larger amounts the DC component can even “blind” it, so that it stops protecting everything else on that circuit as well. That is why charger installations call for a type A RCD with 6 mA DC detection or a type B RCD — not because someone went overboard, but because that is how the physics works.

Kratak odgovor: ako kabl do vašeg mesta: Short answer: if the cable to your space passes through common parts of the building, you need a decision of the residents' assembly (skupština stambene zajednice). As a rule it is taken by a simple majority of those present at a meeting with a quorum, and it takes 4–10 weeks from the request to installation. Assemblies do not say “no” to a charger — they say “no” to an unclear electricity bill and unclear liability. With good paperwork, the conversation is different.
Kratak odgovor: iznajmljena garaža je na: Short answer: a rented garage is the simplest case — no residents' assembly, no vote, just one person who has to say “yes”. The owner says it once they know three things: that they will not be paying for your electricity, that nobody will put their garage at risk, and what happens to the equipment when you move out. All three are settled with one sheet of paper and one meter.
Kratak odgovor: kompletan wallbox 11 kW: Short answer: a complete 11 kW wallbox with installation in Serbia costs about ⟦0⟧–⟦1⟧ RSD including VAT. The difference between quotes is rarely in the device itself — it is almost always in the circuit, the protection, the meter, the test certificate and the paperwork.
Kratak odgovor: punjenje auta nije opasn: Short answer: charging a car is not dangerous — what is dangerous is an ordinary socket under full load for hours. A safe installation has a dedicated circuit, the right cable cross-section, type A RCD protection with DC detection (or type B) and an industrial socket or a fixed wallbox. And the test certificate is the document proving that all of this has been measured — ask for it from anyone who installs a charger for you.
Kratak odgovor: punjenje u zgradi je leg: Short answer: charging in an apartment building is legal and does not require a licence. You need a dedicated circuit with protection, a MID-certified meter and — when the cable runs through the common areas of the building — a decision of the residents' assembly.
Kratak odgovor: sam uređaj od 11 kW u we: Short answer: an 11 kW device on its own costs from about ⟦0⟧ RSD in a web shop, a charger with standard “turnkey” installation ⟦1⟧–⟦2⟧ RSD, and if you buy the device separately, the installation alone typically costs another ⟦3⟧–⟦4⟧ RSD. The only way to make that both fair and verifiable is a separate MID-certified meter on the charger's circuit. Everything else (“guesswork”, a flat fee, a shared socket) stops working after the first winter bill.

MID je evropska direktiva o mernim instr: MID is the European Measuring Instruments Directive (2014/32/EU). A meter with the MID marking is factory-verified for billing: its readings are a valid basis for one party to charge another for electricity. EPS uses exactly this kind of meter too. A meter without that marking — a cheap counter bought online, a “power meter” in the charger's app, a CT sensor for load management — shows an approximate value and is for information, not for billing.

MID is the European Measuring Instruments Directive: a meter with the MID marking is certified for billing — its readings are a valid basis for one party to charge another for electricity. An ordinary meter from a shop or a “power meter” in the charger is for information, not for billing. If you live in an apartment building or rent a garage, a MID-certified meter is the only way for the owner or the residents' assembly to see exactly how much you have used — more in the electricity guide.

Na liniji punjača stoji zasebno sertifik: A separate MID-certified meter is installed on the charger's circuit. It is read once a month, the consumption is multiplied by the kilowatt-hour price from the actual bill of whoever owns the meter the electricity runs through — the garage owner or the building — and the amount is reimbursed with a statement. No markup, no estimates, with a paper trail. This is the only method that owners and building managers accept without resistance, because it creates neither risk nor work for them.

Paušalna zabrana punjenja električnih vo: A blanket ban on charging electric vehicles in the garage has no basis in the regulations — since 2024, charging in garages has been regulated by a dedicated rulebook, not prohibited. But the assembly may turn down a specific request, and a quarrel with the neighbours is the most expensive route. A better route is to change the question: instead of “may I”, propose “how shall we” — a solution for the whole garage that costs the building nothing, in which each user pays for their own space and their own electricity, and the garage gets a plan instead of one-off holes in the wall. Professional building managers recommend exactly this order: specification, electrician's assessment, vote, installation with a test certificate, separate metering.
Paušalne zabrane tipa „u ovoj zgradi je: Blanket bans in the house rules along the lines of “charging electric vehicles is prohibited in this building” can be legally challenged — especially when you put the paperwork on the table: a technical specification, certified metering and a test certificate.

Po <strong>čl. 210v Zakona o energetici<: Under Article 210v of the Energy Law vehicle charging is a service, not a sale of electricity: the service provider is a company or sole trader that buys electricity as a final customer, so it does not need a supply licence. The law provides for the Government to set the technical conditions and metering by decree — according to the available information, that decree has not yet been adopted, so billing per kilowatt-hour “is not possible at the moment” (RTS, ⟦0⟧). That is why operators charge for time.
Po Uredbi o uvozu motornih vozila (čl. 4: Under the Decree on the Import of Motor Vehicles (Article 4), import is permitted if the vehicle was manufactured to at least the Euro 3 standard, and there is no general age limit (the exception is classic cars older than 30 years). For an electric car the exhaust emission standard does not apply because it produces no emissions (spediter.rs). The announced switch to Euro 5 has not been written into the decree — in 2025, ⟦0⟧ used cars with Euro 3 and 4 engines were imported (Bloomberg Adria, ⟦1⟧).

Prodaja električne energije je licencira: Selling electricity is a licensed supply activity — none of us does that, and none of us needs to. What happens in a building's garage or in a rented garage is something else: the electricity still runs through the existing meter (yours, the owner's or the building's), and you reimburse the actual cost to the meter's owner, based on the measured consumption and at the price on their bill, with nothing added. This is cost re-invoicing (prefakturisanje) — the same logic by which a tenant pays for electricity in rented business premises, or the costs of common-area consumption are shared among residents. For a building, it is a cost allocation by decision of the residents' assembly; for a garage owner, an item in the lease agreement.

U iznajmljenoj garaži struja skoro uvek: In a rented garage the electricity almost always goes through the owner's meter. The answer that works: a separate certified MID meter sits on the charger circuit, once a month the owner receives a statement with the reading and the amount at the price on their bill, with no markup, and the reimbursement is paid together with the rent. Without a meter, every arrangement falls apart at the first winter bill. What the billing looks like in practice.
U praksi MID brojilo izgleda kao mali mo: In practice, a MID-certified meter looks like a small module on a DIN rail in the distribution board, with a display and the option of remote reading (Modbus / OCPP). Some chargers have one built into the device itself — all that matters is that it bears the MID marking and an accuracy class (B or 1). Three things a MID-certified meter solves at once:

Ugradnja kućnog punjača nije samo kačenj: Installing a home charger is not just hanging a device on the wall. The electrician runs a dedicated circuit from the distribution board to the charging point, fits the protection devices, connects and sets up the charger and finally tests the installation. That is why the price depends mostly on the distance to the board and on how the cable is run — through the wall, in trunking or along the garage wall. Companies that publish a price usually state what is included in “standard installation” and estimate any additional work on site. If you have already bought a charger, the list also includes electricians who install the device you bring.

Because a Schuko socket is not made for hours of continuous load: during longer charging at 16 A the contacts and the cable heat up, and in an old installation the temperature can rise to a dangerous level. A dedicated circuit with protection solves this once and for all.

Četiri propisa uređuju punjač u garaži z: Four regulations govern a charger in a building's garage. None of them prohibits it; each requires it to be done properly.
Član 210v Zakona o energetici uređuje us: Article 210v of the Energy Law regulates the charging service in public places — your garage is not one. Three things that are nevertheless not allowed, and that you will recognise when someone offers them to you: a markup on the kilowatt-hour (“you'll pay me 15 dinars per kWh” when the bill says 6), a flat-rate “sale” of electricity without a meter, and billing at a tariff that does not come from the actual bill. If the owner wants more money for the use of the space, the right place for that is the rent — not the price of electricity.

Šuko utičnica od 16 A je projektovana za: A 16 A Schuko socket is designed for short-term loads — a vacuum cleaner, a heater, tools. A charger draws 10–16 A continuously, for hours. The contacts heat up, the springs weaken, the contact gets worse and heats up even more — and after half an hour the socket heads towards 100 °C. If it is also on an extension cord, especially one wound on a reel, the cable heats itself up; if the cable is long, the voltage drops along it and the charger runs at its limit.
